subject: Clarify default log holdings: what we keep by default (requests, streamed fragments, KV cache, attachments)
messages:
From: Alice Yang <alice.yang@cedarmed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cedarmed.com
Date: Tue, 03 Dec 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (prompts, outputs, streams)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for walking us through the integration call yesterday. Security has a few follow-ups so we can complete our intake: a short, explicit list of what Redwood stores by default for hosted customers. Specifically: 

- Do you store raw user inputs (prompts) by default?
- Do you store full model outputs (final completions) by default?
- What happens to streamed / partial token fragments that are emitted during generation? Are those preserved anywhere by default?
- Is the KV cache (session-level attention cache) persisted beyond the immediate request?
- How are file attachments handled if they are uploaded as part of a prompt (e.g., PDFs stripped/extracted)?

We'd like a clear one-page answer we can share with our compliance team. We attached our standard questionnaire (cedarmed-q3-questions.pdf) — feel free to reference. Also, do you provide proof of deletion / erasure logs if we request a customer-facing erase?

Thanks,
Alice Yang
Security Program Manager
CedarMed

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Dec 2029 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (prompts, outputs, streams)

Jordan / Marissa — drafting suggested text below. I pulled the language from the hosted default policy (internal doc HS-98765) and kept it short for customer consumption. Please review edits inline, then Jordan can send to CedarMed.

Suggested reply (customer-facing):

"Short answer: For hosted accounts using the default plan, Redwood persists request metadata and final artifacts by default for a limited retention window; streaming fragments and ephemeral internals are not retained as separate long-lived artifacts. We provide erasure workflows and deletion evidence on request."

Bulleted clarifications: 
- "Prompts / user inputs: Persisted by default as request records tied to the invocation. These are retained for 45 days under the hosted default retention window, after which they are deleted automatically.
"
- "Model outputs / final completions: Persisted by default as artifacts and stored for 45 days. If the output is exported to a customer-managed index or storage, Redwood treats that as outside the default retention window.
"
- "Streamed / partial token fragments: Streaming buffers are transient. For hosted default customers we do not persist intermediate token fragments to long-term storage; only the finalized completion is stored. (Operational traces used for debugging are scrubbed and retained per the 45-day telemetry retention policy, with access controls.)
"
- "KV cache / session caches: KV caches are ephemeral runtime artifacts. They are kept in-memory (or on ephemeral NVMe for active serving) and are not written to customer-visible long-term logs by default. They are not part of the 45-day stored request artifacts.
"
- "Attachments / file inputs: Files uploaded as part of a request are retained as request attachments and follow the same 45-day retention window by default. If a customer elects redaction or opt-out at onboarding we can configure that.
"
- "Proof of deletion / erasure evidence: We can provide deletion confirmations tied to our internal purge jobs and an audit trail (job ids, timestamps). For enterprise customers we can provide signed erase reports and coordinate an on-demand export of deletion evidence; this is typically part of a Private or Dedicated contract addendum.

A couple of operational caveats to include if they dig deeper: default window is 45 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private may have different defaults and configurable TTLs. Also note that logs used for debugging/debug traces are accessible only to the ops team and follow a separate telemetry TTL (45 days).

If that looks good I'll trim it to one page and add the link to the hosted policy doc.

—Kimberly
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Yang <alice.yang@cedarmed.com>
Cc: security@cedarmed.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Dec 2029 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default (prompts, outputs, streams)

Hi Alice — thanks for the good questions and for the questionnaire. Below is a concise summary you can share with your compliance team; attached is a one-page PDF summary referencing our hosted defaults.

Concise summary (hosted defaults, US region):
- Prompts / user inputs: Stored by default as part of the request record and retained for 45 days.
- Model outputs (final completions): Stored by default and retained for 45 days.
- Streamed / partial token fragments: Not stored as separate long-lived artifacts; only the final completion is persisted.
- KV cache / session caches: Ephemeral runtime artifacts; not written to long-term logs by default.
- Attachments uploaded with a request: Treated as request attachments and retained for 45 days by default.

Proof of deletion: We can produce deletion evidence (purge job id, timestamp, and audit log reference). For enterprise customers we provide signed erase reports upon request; we can coordinate this if CedarMed needs one for your records.

If you want, Kimberly can provide the internal policy link and we can set up a short call to walk through the questionnaire items.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
